model.dcode212_academique.fct_performanc.name: fct_performance_academique
model.dcode212_academique.fct_performanc.description: Table de faits : une ligne par évaluation. Grain = id_note.
model.dcode212_academique.fct_performanc.raw_code:
with notes as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_notes') }}
),
cours as (
    select id_cours, id_formation, id_annee, credits_ects from {{ ref('stg_cours') }}
)
select
    n.id_note,
    n.id_etudiant,
    n.id_cours,
    c.id_formation,
    n.id_annee,
    n.type_evaluation,
    n.note,
    c.credits_ects,
    n.date_evaluation,
    case
        when n.note < 10 then 'Insuffisant'
        when n.note < 12 then 'Passable'
        when n.note < 14 then 'Assez Bien'
        when n.note < 16 then 'Bien'
        else 'Très Bien'
    end                     as mention,
    (n.note >= 10)          as est_validee
from notes n
left join cours c on n.id_cours = c.id_cours

model.dcode212_academique.int_etudiants_.name: int_etudiants_enrichis
model.dcode212_academique.int_etudiants_.description: Étudiants enrichis avec âge, tranche d'âge, nom complet ; dédoublonnés.
model.dcode212_academique.int_etudiants_.raw_code:
with etudiants as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_etudiants') }}
),
dedupliques as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (partition by id_etudiant order by id_etudiant) as rn
    from etudiants
    where id_etudiant is not null
),
enrichis as (
    select
        id_etudiant,
        matricule,
        nom,
        prenom,
        nom || ' ' || prenom                                        as nom_complet,
        date_naissance,
        date_part('year', age(current_date, date_naissance))::int   as age,
        sexe,
        nationalite,
        email,
        date_premiere_inscription,
        statut
    from dedupliques
    where rn = 1
)
select
    *,
    case
        when age < 20 then '18-19'
        when age < 23 then '20-22'
        when age < 26 then '23-25'
        else '26+'
    end as tranche_age
from enrichis

model.dcode212_academique.int_cours_enri.name: int_cours_enrichis
model.dcode212_academique.int_cours_enri.description: Cours joints à leur formation, enseignant et période académique.
model.dcode212_academique.int_cours_enri.raw_code:
with cours as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_cours') }}
),
formations as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_formations_enrichies') }}
),
enseignants as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_enseignants_enrichis') }}
),
annees as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_annees_academiques') }}
)
select
    c.id_cours,
    c.code_cours,
    c.intitule,
    c.credits_ects,
    c.volume_horaire,
    f.id_formation,
    f.nom_formation,
    f.nom_departement,
    ens.id_enseignant,
    ens.nom_complet    as nom_enseignant,
    ens.grade          as grade_enseignant,
    a.id_annee,
    a.libelle          as annee_academique,
    a.semestre
from cours c
left join formations f  on c.id_formation  = f.id_formation
left join enseignants ens on c.id_enseignant = ens.id_enseignant
left join annees a      on c.id_annee       = a.id_annee

model.dcode212_academique.int_notes_enri.name: int_notes_enrichies
model.dcode212_academique.int_notes_enri.description: Notes enrichies avec mention calculée, statut de validation, et contexte complet.
model.dcode212_academique.int_notes_enri.raw_code:
with notes as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_notes') }}
),
etudiants as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_etudiants_enrichis') }}
),
cours as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_cours_enrichis') }}
),
enrichies as (
    select
        n.id_note,
        n.type_evaluation,
        n.note,
        n.date_evaluation,
        e.id_etudiant,
        e.nom_complet     as nom_etudiant,
        e.tranche_age,
        e.sexe,
        c.id_cours,
        c.intitule        as intitule_cours,
        c.credits_ects,
        c.nom_formation,
        c.nom_departement,
        c.nom_enseignant,
        c.annee_academique,
        c.semestre
    from notes n
    left join etudiants e on n.id_etudiant = e.id_etudiant
    left join cours c     on n.id_cours    = c.id_cours
)
select
    *,
    case
        when note < 10 then 'Insuffisant'
        when note < 12 then 'Passable'
        when note < 14 then 'Assez Bien'
        when note < 16 then 'Bien'
        else 'Très Bien'
    end                     as mention,
    (note >= 10)            as est_validee
from enrichies

model.dcode212_academique.int_inscriptio.name: int_inscriptions_enrichies
model.dcode212_academique.int_inscriptio.description: Inscriptions jointes aux étudiants et formations, avec contexte démographique.
model.dcode212_academique.int_inscriptio.raw_code:
with inscriptions as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_inscriptions') }}
),
etudiants as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_etudiants_enrichis') }}
),
formations as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_formations_enrichies') }}
),
annees as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_annees_academiques') }}
)
select
    i.id_inscription,
    i.date_inscription,
    i.statut_inscription,
    i.mode,
    e.id_etudiant,
    e.nom_complet          as nom_etudiant,
    e.tranche_age,
    e.sexe,
    e.statut               as statut_etudiant,
    f.id_formation,
    f.nom_formation,
    f.nom_departement,
    a.id_annee,
    a.libelle              as annee_academique,
    a.semestre
from inscriptions i
left join etudiants e  on i.id_etudiant  = e.id_etudiant
left join formations f on i.id_formation = f.id_formation
left join annees a     on i.id_annee     = a.id_annee

{% macro postgres__list_relations_without_caching(schema_relation) %}
  {% call statement('list_relations_without_caching', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      tablename as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'table' as type
    from pg_tables
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      viewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'view' as type
    from pg_views
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      matviewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'materialized_view' as type
    from pg_matviews
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select distinct
     '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
     proname as name,
     ns.nspname as schema,
     'function' as type
    from pg_proc
     join pg_namespace as ns on pronamespace = ns.oid
    where ns.nspname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
  {% endcall %}
  {{ return(load_result('list_relations_without_caching').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

{% macro postgres__get_show_indexes_sql(relation) %}
    select
        i.relname                                   as name,
        m.amname                                    as method,
        ix.indisunique                              as "unique",
        array_to_string(array_agg(a.attname), ',')  as column_names
    from pg_index ix
    join pg_class i
        on i.oid = ix.indexrelid
    join pg_am m
        on m.oid=i.relam
    join pg_class t
        on t.oid = ix.indrelid
    join pg_namespace n
        on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    join pg_attribute a
        on a.attrelid = t.oid
        and a.attnum = ANY(ix.indkey)
    where t.relname = '{{ relation.identifier }}'
      and n.nspname = '{{ relation.schema }}'
      and t.relkind in ('r', 'm')
    group by 1, 2, 3
    order by 1, 2, 3

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.name: postgres__get_relations
macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_relations() -%}

  {#
      -- in pg_depend, objid is the dependent, refobjid is the referenced object
      --  > a pg_depend entry indicates that the referenced object cannot be
      --  > dropped without also dropping the dependent object.
  #}

  {%- call statement('relations', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select distinct
        dependent_namespace.nspname as dependent_schema,
        dependent_class.relname as dependent_name,
        referenced_namespace.nspname as referenced_schema,
        referenced_class.relname as referenced_name

    -- Query for views: views are entries in pg_class with an entry in pg_rewrite, but we avoid
    -- a seq scan on pg_rewrite by leveraging the fact there is an "internal" row in pg_depend for
    -- the view...
    from pg_class as dependent_class
    join pg_namespace as dependent_namespace on dependent_namespace.oid = dependent_class.relnamespace
    join pg_depend as dependent_depend on dependent_depend.refobjid = dependent_class.oid
        and dependent_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.deptype = 'i'

    -- ... and via pg_depend (that has a row per column, hence the need for "distinct" above, and
    -- making sure to exclude the internal row to avoid a view appearing to depend on itself)...
    join pg_depend as joining_depend on joining_depend.objid = dependent_depend.objid
        and joining_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refobjid != dependent_depend.refobjid

    -- ... we can find the tables they query from in pg_class, but excluding system tables. Note we
    -- don't need need to exclude _dependent_ system tables, because they only query from other
    -- system tables, and so are automatically excluded by excluding _referenced_ system tables
    join pg_class as referenced_class on referenced_class.oid = joining_depend.refobjid
    join pg_namespace as referenced_namespace on referenced_namespace.oid = referenced_class.relnamespace
        and referenced_namespace.nspname != 'information_schema'
        and referenced_namespace.nspname not like 'pg\_%'

    order by
        dependent_schema, dependent_name, referenced_schema, referenced_name;

  {%- endcall -%}

  {{ return(load_result('relations').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

---

### More information

- Read the [dbt viewpoint](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/viewpoint)
- [Installation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/installation)
- Join the [dbt Community](https://www.getdbt.com/community/) for questions and discussion
